Bedzin New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Będzin, Poland

Demolished. Będzin's third Jewish cemetery, founded in the 1890s in the Warpie neighborhood, filled up by WWI, prompting the community to establish a newer cemetery in neighboring Czeladź; individual burials nonetheless continued here until WWII (see the Będzin Old Jewish Cemetery record for the town's fuller community history, including its 30,000-person ghetto and near-total destruction by 1943). Germans destroyed the cemetery during the war; from 1943 to mid-1946 the land was incorporated into the 'Eltes' stone quarry. Late-1960s municipal plans expanded a local bus terminal onto the site - some tombstones were rescued beforehand and moved to the old cemetery, with additional exhumed remains relocated to Czeladź, though many stones were paved over or repurposed for a nearby overpass. Further recovered tombstones were relocated to Podzamcze Street in 2008 by Adam Szydłowski.
